entries.title: A day with western lowland gorillas
entries.answer: Western lowland gorillas live in forests in central Africa. They walk on the ground a great deal, often resting their weight on their knuckles. They also climb and reach for food in trees. A gorilla group spends part of the day moving among places where it can eat fruit, leaves, and stems. A mature male often leads the group. He can be recognized by the lighter hair that grows across his back, giving rise to the name silverback.
facts: Gorillas are great apes.
Some gorillas eat insects as well as plants.

questions.text: How does an orangutan spend more time far above the ground?
How does a sloth rest safely in a tree?
Which other large mammal eats mostly plants?

entries.title: A ferret that depends on prairie dogs
entries.answer: A black-footed ferret may spend much of the day underground in tunnels dug by prairie dogs. It also hunts prairie dogs for food, following them through narrow passages where larger animals could not fit. When wide areas of prairie were lost and many prairie dog colonies disappeared, black-footed ferrets became very rare. A small group found in Wyoming helped people raise ferrets for release. Recovery requires land with enough prairie dogs to feed wild ferrets and provide burrows.
facts: Black-footed ferrets usually hunt at night.
The black-footed ferret is the only ferret native to North America.

questions.text: How do rodents make tunnels for a whole colony?
What happens when a different rodent builds shelters other species use?
What changes when one kind of animal depends on another?

entries.title: A giant lizard from Indonesian islands
entries.answer: The Komodo dragon is a real animal found on a few islands in Indonesia. It is the largest kind of lizard alive today. A Komodo dragon flicks its tongue out and picks up tiny traces from the air. Inside its mouth, an organ helps it read those traces and find food. Young dragons often spend time in trees, where they are safer from larger Komodo dragons. Heavy adults spend most of their time on the ground.
facts: Large Komodo dragons can be about ten feet long.
Komodo dragons have forked tongues.

questions.text: What large reptile swims using its tail?
How does a big cat chase prey in open places?
How do the animals on an island affect one another?

entries.title: A red panda’s life in the trees
entries.answer: Look carefully at a branch in an Asian mountain forest and a red panda might be resting around it. This small mammal has reddish fur and a ringed tail. It can use its bushy tail to help balance and curl it around its body in cold weather. Much of its food is bamboo, even though it belongs to a different animal family from the giant panda. Red pandas grip branches as they climb with curved claws.
facts: Red pandas can climb down a tree headfirst.
Red pandas have a thumb-like wrist bone that helps them grasp bamboo.

questions.text: How does a giant panda hold bamboo?
What other mammals spend much of life in trees?
How do large apes travel between tree branches?

entries.title: Bats and how they find their way
entries.answer: Bats are mammals and can fly by flapping their wings. Their wings are made of thin skin stretched over long fingers. Many kinds of bats fly in the dark and use sound to find their way. A bat makes a call and listens for the sound to bounce back. The echo may tell the bat where a moth or a branch is. This is called echolocation. Bats can also see. Many eat insects, but some kinds eat fruit or drink nectar from flowers.
facts: Bats are the only mammals that can fly by flapping their wings.
Some bats can carry pollen between flowers.

questions.text: How can a sound wave bounce off something and come back?
How do animals help flowers make seeds?
How can a change that helps an animal spread through a group over time?

entries.title: Can a porcupine throw its quills?
entries.answer: A North American porcupine does not toss its quills across the air. The quills are stiff hairs that come loose if an animal bumps into them. Tiny hooks near their tips can hold them in place after they stick. Before that happens, the porcupine can raise its quills and turn its back toward danger. It often climbs trees to eat leaves, buds, or bark. When it is feeding quietly, the quills may lie fairly flat.
facts: Porcupines grow new quills if old ones come loose.
A North American porcupine is a rodent.

questions.text: Which other rodent uses its teeth on tree bark?
How does a different tree climber protect itself from the cold?
How does a frog warn other animals to leave it alone?

entries.title: How a beaver makes a pond
entries.answer: A beaver can turn a shallow stream into a pond by piling branches and mud across it. Water slows down behind the dam and spreads into a wider area. That water helps a beaver move branches and swim safely to its home. A home built from sticks and mud is called a lodge. It can have an opening under the pond’s surface. Other animals can find food and shelter in the wet ground and open water created by a beaver dam.
facts: Beavers gnaw through branches with strong front teeth.
A lodge is a beaver’s home. A dam holds water back.

questions.text: Where might water go after leaving a beaver pond?
What other animal changes a wetland by digging?
How does another animal use homes made by its neighbors?

entries.title: How an alligator lives on land and in water
entries.answer: An American alligator can float with much of its body hidden below the surface. Its eyes and nostrils sit high enough to stay above the water while it waits. A strong tail helps it swim in marshes, ponds, and rivers. Alligators can dig deep places that hold water when a wetland dries out. Fish and other animals may gather in those holes during dry times, so an alligator can help shape the wetland it lives in.
facts: American alligators live in the southeastern United States.
A mother alligator guards her nest and can protect her young.

questions.text: How can a dam make a wet area bigger?
How does another large reptile hunt on land?
What happens to water in a marsh when the weather stays dry?

entries.title: How can a barn swallow build a nest from drops of mud?
entries.answer: A barn swallow can pick up little lumps of damp earth and carry them to a sheltered nesting spot. It adds the mud bit by bit against a steady surface until it forms an open nest cup. Bits of grass can be mixed in to help hold the pieces together. A roof or bridge above it can keep heavy rain off the new nest. Once the cup dries, the birds put softer material inside.
facts: Barn swallows often have deeply forked tails.

questions.text: What different material does a chimney swift use to fasten a nest to a wall?
How can a bird make a bag that hangs from twigs?
Why do different birds choose different places to nest?

entries.title: How can a barred owl find food in the dark?
entries.answer: A barred owl often hunts from a branch near a clear spot in the woods. It can listen for a small animal moving in the leaves and use its large eyes when there is some light. Soft edges on owl wing feathers can help make flight quieter. From the branch, the owl can drop toward the sound. A barred owl may also call after dark with a series of hoots.
facts: People often remember one barred owl call as sounding like the words “Who cooks for you?”

questions.text: How does a fox use sound to find hidden mice?
Why can it be hard for people to see color in dim light?
Why can lights at night affect birds traveling above a city?

entries.title: How can a blue jay carry more than one acorn?
entries.answer: A blue jay does not have to carry every acorn by the tip of its bill. It has room in its throat to hold some food while it travels. A jay can carry nuts from under an oak to another place, where it can hide them for later. Some buried nuts never get eaten. If one stays in a good patch of soil, a young oak may grow far from its parent tree.
facts: Besides acorns and other nuts, blue jays can eat seeds and small animals such as insects.

questions.text: Why does a gray squirrel bury a nut in the ground?
What are some other ways seeds travel?
How does a chickadee save seeds for later?

entries.title: How can a crack in a tree trunk be a tiny hiding place?
entries.answer: From a distance, an older tree trunk looks mostly solid. Close up, it may have thin cracks, bumps, and little roof-like pieces of bark. Some small animals can fit in the narrow spaces. The tree can also have dead spots where insects have left tunnels in the wood. A bird that looks closely from one crack to the next may find food hidden from an animal watching from farther away.
facts: You can see ordinary bark hiding places without lifting bark off a live tree.

questions.text: How does a brown creeper search for food in bark cracks?
What other places for animals can form in a dead trunk?
How can a woodpecker reach food on a tree?

entries.title: How can a mockingbird sound like more than one kind of bird?
entries.answer: A northern mockingbird can learn parts of other sounds and fit them into its own song. It may repeat one short sound several times, then switch to a different one. If you hear what seems like several kinds of bird from a single high branch, watch that branch to see whether one bird makes all the sounds. A mockingbird with a long gray tail and flashes of white in its wings can be easier to recognize once you see it.
facts: A copied sound can be only a short part of a longer performance.

questions.text: How do your ears tell high notes from low ones?
How can you tell which branch a sound is coming from?
How can a sound travel from a high branch to your ears?

entries.title: How can a red-backed salamander breathe without lungs?
entries.answer: An eastern red-backed salamander has no lungs. Oxygen can pass into its body across its moist skin and the lining of its mouth. When the ground gets dry, the salamander may hide beneath a damp log or stone. Unlike many salamanders, this kind does not need a pond for its young to swim in. Its eggs can hatch into tiny land-living salamanders in a moist hiding place.
facts: Some eastern red-backed salamanders lack the red stripe that gives the species its name.

questions.text: Why does a spotted salamander need a pool for its young?
What else grows or lives around a fallen log?
Why can a wood frog survive cold that would harm many animals?

entries.title: How can a river otter look for food in the dark water?
entries.answer: A North American river otter can feel changes in the water with long whiskers around its mouth. A fish or another small animal moving nearby can make ripples that the whiskers help detect. The otter also has webbed feet and a long strong tail for moving through water. It can close its nostrils as it dives. River otters can also travel out of the water across shorelines between places to feed.
facts: A thick coat helps keep a river otter warm in cold water.

questions.text: How does an otter that lives along a coast affect a kelp forest?
Why are some fish more common in cool streams?
What can trees or shrubs change about a river's edge?

entries.title: How can a ruby-throated hummingbird stop in midair?
entries.answer: A ruby-throated hummingbird can beat its wings rapidly while keeping its body nearly in one spot. Its wings sweep back and forth and turn between strokes, helping the bird stay up without moving ahead. Hovering lets it put its slender bill into a flower that cannot hold its weight. The bird takes sweet nectar with its tongue. It also catches small insects and spiders for part of its food.
facts: The bright patch on an adult male’s throat can appear dark when it catches the light at a different angle.

questions.text: How does an animal carry pollen between flowers?
How can an osprey use flight to catch fish?
How do wings hold up an airplane?

entries.title: How can a tufted titmouse use one foot to help open a seed?
entries.answer: At a feeder, a tufted titmouse may take one seed and fly away rather than open it where it finds it. On a branch it can use a foot to pin the seed down. Then its beak can tap or pry at the shell without the seed rolling away. Sometimes the bird carries a seed off and hides it in a food cache. Look for the small gray crest sticking up on its head.
facts: Tufted titmice also eat insects and other small foods.

questions.text: What does a nuthatch use instead of a foot to steady a seed?
How can hiding food help a bird later?
Why do many other seed-eating birds have a thick bill?

entries.title: How can a water strider stand on water?
entries.answer: Water molecules attract one another. At the surface, that attraction makes it harder for something to break through, a property called surface tension. The long legs of a water strider spread its weight across the surface. Tiny hairs on the legs help keep them from getting wet. An insect can press tiny dimples into the water and still stay on top as it pushes itself forward.
facts: Water striders can use their legs to sense small waves made by prey near the surface.

questions.text: What is a dragonfly nymph doing beneath the water?
Why can many plants grow in a pond’s shallows?
How can ice float on water?

entries.title: How can you tell a damselfly from a dragonfly?
entries.answer: A resting damselfly usually holds its four wings together above or along its body. Many dragonflies rest with theirs pointing out to the sides. A damselfly usually has a thin body and eyes that look widely spaced. These clues work for many kinds, but not for all of them. Some damselflies, for instance, can rest with their wings partly open. Both kinds of insect begin life in water.
facts: The front and back wings of a damselfly are usually more similar in shape than the front and back wings of a dragonfly.

questions.text: What happens when a young dragonfly leaves the water?
Why can some insects walk on the top of the water?
How do wings hold up an airplane?

entries.title: How do California mussels stick to a rocky shore?
entries.answer: A California mussel makes strong threads that fasten its shell to a rock or to other mussels. Waves can pull hard on the shell without sweeping it away. Many mussels end up packed together in a dark patch called a mussel bed. When covered with water, a mussel draws water through its body and catches tiny food in it. Taking food out of water this way is called filter feeding. If the rock becomes dry, the mussel can shut its two shells tightly.
facts: Small animals can shelter in the gaps between the shells of a mussel bed.

questions.text: How does a sea star use its feet to pull on a mussel?
How does a freshwater mussel grow up?
When are rocks uncovered on a shore?

entries.title: How does a Baltimore oriole hang its nest from thin branches?
entries.answer: A Baltimore oriole makes a hanging nest that can look like a small cloth bag. The female works narrow strands around twigs and around other strands. She adds more until the walls form a pouch below the points that hold it. The eggs and young can sit inside, while the outside can move when the twigs sway. A lining of softer material covers the woven structure near the bottom.
facts: The nest often hangs near the tip of a branch.

questions.text: How does a swallow build a cup from mud rather than weaving fibers?
How does a house wren make a nest inside a hole?
What kinds of support hold nests for different birds?

entries.title: How does a barnacle live stuck to a rock?
entries.answer: An acorn barnacle starts life swimming in the sea. Later it settles on a hard surface and sticks there. The adult grows a set of hard plates around its body. When seawater covers it, plates at the top can open. The barnacle sweeps feathery legs out of the opening to catch tiny drifting animals and other plankton. When the shore is exposed, closing the plates helps keep its body from drying out.
facts: A barnacle is a crustacean, in the same large group of animals as crabs and shrimp.

questions.text: Why does the upper shore stay out of water longer than the lower shore?
How does a sea snail grip a rock?
What tiny living things drift in seawater?

entries.title: How does a box turtle shut the opening in its shell?
entries.answer: An eastern box turtle can draw its head, tail, and feet into its shell when danger is close. Underneath the turtle is a movable joint called a shell hinge. The turtle can raise sections of the lower shell to close the gaps, a little like moving the lid shut on a small box. It then has less soft body exposed. This works differently from a snapping turtle's smaller lower shell.
facts: Eastern box turtles spend much of their time on land.

questions.text: Why can't a snapping turtle close up in the same way?
Where does a painted turtle go to warm up in the sun?
What job does a door hinge have that is similar to this turtle's shell hinge?

entries.title: How does a chain pickerel hide while it waits for food?
entries.answer: A chain pickerel can wait in or near water plants with most of its long body barely moving. If a small fish swims within reach, the pickerel can dart forward. Waiting near plants can help it avoid being noticed. Dark marks along its sides connect into shapes that look like a chain. You may see this pattern more easily than the fish itself when it emerges into open water.
facts: The chain pickerel and northern pike belong to the same family, but are different kinds of fish.

questions.text: Why does a great blue heron stand still before catching fish?
How does a bluegill prepare a nest in a shallow place?
Why can plants grow under the water near the edge of a pond?

entries.title: How does a chickadee save food for later?
entries.answer: A black-capped chickadee can take one seed and fly off to tuck it away in a small hiding place. It may hide food in many separate spots, such as cracks in bark. Later it can remember where each food cache is and go back when it needs a meal. The bird is small but can stay through the winter in much of its range. It eats insects as well as seeds and other plant food.
facts: A black-capped chickadee can hide a food item in a different spot from the one it used for its last item.

questions.text: Which squirrel also uses separate hiding spots?
How can a blue jay carry more than one nut?
Why do some people look for wildlife in a park as part of a bioblitz?

entries.title: How does a giant anteater eat without teeth?
entries.answer: A giant anteater has a long, narrow face and no teeth. When it finds an ant or termite nest, it can rake open a small spot with its front claws. It reaches inside with a long tongue coated with sticky spit. Insects cling to the tongue and are pulled into the mouth as the tongue flicks back and forth. An anteater moves among nests rather than emptying one nest at a time.
facts: A giant anteater’s tongue can reach roughly two feet.
Its front claws are long, so it bends them out of the way when it walks.

questions.text: How does a relative of the anteater use curved claws?
Which other mammal digs for insects?
How does an animal’s body break food down after swallowing it?

entries.title: How does a limpet hold on to a rock?
entries.answer: A limpet is a sea snail with a shell shaped a little like a low hat. A broad, muscular foot spreads under it. The foot gives the limpet a strong grip when waves wash across a rock. Many limpets crawl across the rock as they feed, using a rough tongue-like part to scrape up a thin layer of algae. From above, a resting limpet may look like part of the rock.
facts: Some limpets press their shell down close to the rock when the tide is out, which helps keep moisture in.

questions.text: Which rock animal sweeps food into its mouth with feathery legs?
Why is one part of a rocky shore drier than another?
Which shore animal holds on with threads?

entries.title: How does a nuthatch look for food going down a tree?
entries.answer: A white-breasted nuthatch can grip the rough surface of a tree and head straight down with its beak first. The bird stops to check gaps in the bark for food. Going down can give it a different view of the cracks than a bird climbing up would have. You may also see a nuthatch push a seed into a snug gap, then hammer it with its beak instead of dropping it.
facts: White-breasted nuthatches can store some food for later.

questions.text: Which small bird often goes upward along a trunk instead?
What does a woodpecker look for when it checks bark?
How does a chickadee save food for later?

entries.title: How does a raccoon use its front paws?
entries.answer: A raccoon has five long toes on each front paw. It can use the toes to turn food around, feel along the ground, and pick up small things. The paws are sensitive to touch, which helps when a raccoon searches under leaves or in shallow water. A raccoon may handle food in water, but it can also find and eat its meal on dry ground. Many raccoons look for food after dark.
facts: Raccoons eat many kinds of foods, including fruit, insects, and animals they find in shallow water.

questions.text: Which night animal can carry babies in a pouch?
How does a fox find a small animal it cannot see?
What can shore crabs use for daytime shelter?

entries.title: How does a red fox catch prey it cannot see?
entries.answer: A mouse can move under grass or snow without showing itself. A red fox may stop, tilt its head, and listen. Its ears can pick up small sounds that suggest where the animal is moving. The fox can leap into the air and come down with its front paws near the spot it heard. Foxes also eat things they do not have to pounce on, including fruit and insects.
facts: A red fox’s bushy tail often has a white tip.

questions.text: How does an eastern cottontail escape into cover?
What can help a barred owl hunt when the woods are dark?
How does a food web show routes from food to animals?

entries.title: How does a sea anemone catch food?
entries.answer: A sea anemone can look like a flower, with a ring of soft tentacles around the center. It is an animal that eats other animals. Tiny cells on its tentacles can sting prey that brushes past. The tentacles help move food toward the mouth in the middle. Some anemones on rocky shores draw their soft parts inward when the tide goes out. Water covers it again when the tide comes in.
facts: Sea anemones and the tiny animals that build coral reefs belong to the same large group of animals.

questions.text: How do tiny coral animals build a whole reef?
What is a tide pool?
What helps a sea star walk over rocks?

entries.title: How does a sea lion walk on a beach?
entries.answer: A California sea lion can turn its back flippers forward and use them to walk on land. That makes it easier to move around on a beach or a rocky shore. In the water it pushes forward with long front flippers. Look for the small flaps behind the eyes. These are its outer ears, which a true seal lacks. California sea lions also make loud barking calls when many of them gather together.
facts: California sea lions live along the western coast of North America.
An adult male is generally much larger than an adult female.

questions.text: How does a true seal move without turning its back flippers forward?
How does a dolphin swim differently from a sea lion?
What happens when ocean water reaches a rocky shore?

entries.title: How does a striped skunk give a warning?
entries.answer: A striped skunk often tries to make a threat back away before using its strong-smelling spray. It can stamp its front feet and lift its tail. If it needs to defend itself, it can direct a spray from glands below the tail. The skunk’s black-and-white coat stands out even in dim light. An animal that has met a skunk before may recognize its pattern and keep its distance.
facts: The shape and width of the white stripes can differ from one striped skunk to another.

questions.text: Which animal can look as if it has stopped moving completely when threatened?
How does a deer signal danger as it bounds away?
What color helps a cottontail blend into leaves?

entries.title: How does a two-toed sloth live upside down?
entries.answer: A two-toed sloth can spend hours hanging from branches in a tropical forest. Its long, curved claws hook over a branch like handles, and strong limbs help hold it in place. It moves slowly through the leaves to feed and rest. Moving slowly and using little energy help on a diet made mostly of plants. A two-toed sloth has two long claws on each front foot, but three on each of its back feet.
facts: A two-toed sloth can swim.
The outer coat can look greenish when algae grow on the hair.

questions.text: How does a much larger animal get around in trees?
Which tree climber has a bushy tail for balance?
What does a sloth’s relative eat?

entries.title: How does a wood frog survive part of its body freezing?
entries.answer: A wood frog can spend the winter under leaves near the ground. As its surroundings get cold, some water outside its cells can turn to ice. Its body can send extra sugar to its tissues, which helps protect its cells. The frog’s breathing and heartbeat can stop for a time. If conditions stay within what the frog can survive, it can begin moving again after it thaws.
facts: A wood frog has a dark patch that runs through each eye and can look like part of a mask.

questions.text: How can a groundhog get through the cold months underground?
Why do some seasonal pools hold water early in the year?
What can make frozen water less dense than liquid water?

entries.title: How does an Asian elephant use its trunk?
entries.answer: An Asian elephant can pull a branch close, pick up a tiny object, and raise a load of water with the same tool: its trunk. A trunk is an extended nose and upper lip. It bends and twists because it is made of muscle instead of bone. The elephant can suck up water and then pour it into its mouth. It also smells with its trunk and reaches out with it to touch other elephants.
facts: Some male Asian elephants have long tusks. Female Asian elephants usually have much smaller ones or none.
Elephants spend many hours each day feeding on plants.

questions.text: What other mammal uses a long snout to find food?
How does another big mammal grip its food?
How can muscles pull parts of a body into motion?

entries.title: How does an eastern chipmunk carry so many seeds?
entries.answer: A chipmunk has a cheek pouch on each side of its mouth that can stretch. The pouches hold several small seeds to the sides until it can put them down. When it reaches its burrow, the chipmunk can drop the seeds into a storage space. Then it can go out for another load. In cold weather, a chipmunk can wake up from periods of deep rest and eat from what it stored.
facts: An eastern chipmunk’s burrow can have separate places for sleeping and storing food.

questions.text: Why does a gray squirrel put nuts in separate hiding places?
How does a groundhog spend the winter underground?
Which small bird remembers places where it hides food?

entries.title: How does an eastern cottontail stay close to cover?
entries.answer: An eastern cottontail often feeds on grass or low plants near a tangle of bushes. If something startles it, the rabbit can bolt into thick cover where a larger animal may have trouble following. The rabbit’s brownish back helps it blend into leaves and dry grass while it sits still. Its little tail has a white underside that can flash as it runs away. That fluffy white patch gives cottontails their name.
facts: A cottontail often feeds around dawn or dusk, though it may come out at other times.

questions.text: Which animal raises a white tail when alarmed?
How can a fox catch prey when the animal is hidden?
What makes the edge of a forest a good place for some animals?

entries.title: How does an orangutan move in a forest?
entries.answer: Orangutans spend much of their lives above the ground in the forests of Borneo and Sumatra. Their long arms help them reach for branches, and their hands and feet can hold on from different angles. An orangutan may bend a branch toward itself to make the next tree easier to reach. Fruit is an important food. At night, an orangutan can fold leaves and branches together to make a nest that supports its weight well above the ground.
facts: Orangutans are great apes.
A mother orangutan cares for her young for years.

questions.text: How do some great apes spend more time near the ground?
Which other mammal rests high in a forest?
Which bear also depends on forests to find food?

entries.title: How does an osprey keep hold of a slippery fish?
entries.answer: An osprey can spot a fish near the surface while flying over water. It drops down and extends its feet to grab the fish. It can turn an outer toe backward, so two toes grip on each side. Curved claws and rough patches on the feet help it hold on. After the bird rises again, it often carries the fish head first, lined up with its own flight.
facts: Fish make up almost all of an osprey’s food.

questions.text: Which long-legged bird catches fish while standing in shallow water?
How do wings hold up an airplane?
Which fish from the Atlantic also spends part of its life in a river?

entries.title: How lions live and hunt together
entries.answer: Lions often spend time in groups called prides. Females in a pride are often related, and they may care for cubs together. When several lions hunt, each may take a different position around the animals they are approaching. Living in a group also helps lions defend an area that has food and places to rest. Other big cats live differently. A tiger usually looks for food by itself and does not spend its whole life in a group like a pride.
facts: Most wild lions live in Africa, and some live in India.
Adult male lions often grow a mane around the head and neck.

questions.text: How does a tiger hunt when it is on its own?
Which big cat is built for a fast sprint?
How does a group of much smaller mammals work together?

entries.title: Is a horseshoe crab really a crab?
entries.answer: A horseshoe crab has a hard curved shell and a pointed tail. It belongs to a group more closely related to spiders than to true crabs. Its tail helps it turn over if it gets stuck upside down. On some coasts, adults crawl onto sandy beaches to lay and fertilize eggs. Shorebirds can eat exposed eggs, so a beach where the animals gather can also be an important stop for birds.
facts: The shell of a horseshoe crab helps protect legs that are hidden when you view the animal from above.

questions.text: What other food can wading birds find below the mud?
Why does a true hermit crab carry a snail shell?
What is the intertidal zone?

entries.title: Life underground for naked mole-rats
entries.answer: A naked mole-rat lives in a network of tunnels beneath dry ground in eastern Africa. Its large front teeth stick out in front of its lips, so the animal can chew into dirt without filling its mouth with soil. Groups of mole-rats work in a colony. They extend tunnels, gather roots, or guard the openings. A breeding female and a small number of males have the colony’s young. The other animals do much of the digging and food carrying.
facts: Naked mole-rats are rodents.
Their nearly bare skin has a few hairs that help them feel around.

questions.text: Which mammal lives in tunnels built by prairie dogs?
Why are the tunnels used by meerkat groups useful?
How can another rodent reshape the place it lives in?

entries.title: What bird digs a nesting tunnel into a dirt bank?
entries.answer: A belted kingfisher can make a nesting tunnel in a steep bank of sand or soil. The bird can dig into the bank and move loosened grains out as the tunnel gets deeper. The eggs lie in a wider chamber at the back. You may see the same kingfisher on a branch near the water, sitting still until it spots a fish and plunges down. Its nest site and hunting site can be quite close.
facts: A kingfisher can also stop and hover briefly above water before diving.

questions.text: How does an osprey hold a fish caught from above?
What are other kinds of openings birds use for nests?
How does a heron wait before catching a fish?

entries.title: What does a peregrine falcon do before a fast dive?
entries.answer: A peregrine falcon can gain height before diving at a bird below. It then tips into a steep drop and can bring its wings closer to its body. That shape helps it pick up speed on the way down. This steep hunting dive is called a stoop. Peregrines often nest on high ledges. In some cities, the ledge of a tall building can serve a similar purpose to a cliff.
facts: A peregrine is especially fast in a dive, not because it always flies that fast.

What changes when a wing moves through air?
Why can some birds use buildings instead of cliffs or trees?

entries.title: What gives the emperor tamarin its mustached look?
entries.answer: A bearded emperor tamarin is a small monkey with long white whiskers that curve away from its face. Groups move through trees in parts of the western Amazon, eating things like ripe fruit and insects. Its long tail helps balance it during quick movements through branches. Adult males and other group members can help care for young monkeys. A tiny tamarin can ride on an adult’s back before it grows large enough to move easily with the group.
facts: Emperor tamarins are monkeys, rather than apes.
The whiskers gave this monkey its well-known mustached appearance.

questions.text: How is moving through a forest different for a large ape?
How does a different tree dweller use its tail?
Which large ape also lives in forest groups?

entries.title: What helps a sea star walk over rocks?
entries.answer: Look under an arm of a sea star and you may see rows of short, soft parts called tube feet. Water inside a system of channels helps move the feet. One group of feet can attach while others reach for a new spot. Working together, they let the sea star creep across a rock. Some sea stars also use their feet to pull on the two halves of a mussel shell when they are feeding.
facts: A sea star is an animal without a backbone. It is not a fish.

questions.text: How do California mussels stick together?
What else lives in a tide pool?
How can an octopus squeeze between rocks?

entries.title: What helps a tiger hide?
entries.answer: A tiger’s orange and black coat can be hard to make out in tall grass or in a forest with patches of sunlight and shade. Dark stripes break up the shape of its body. This helps a tiger get close to other animals before they notice it. Tigers usually hunt alone and can swim well. They live in several very different parts of Asia, from cold forests in the north to warm islands in the south.
facts: Tigers have their own stripe patterns, so researchers can tell individuals apart in photos.
Tigers can swim across rivers.

questions.text: Why do some big cats work in a group?
How does a cat that chases in the open catch its food?
What large reptile lives on only a few islands?

entries.title: What is a lady beetle looking for on a plant?
entries.answer: Many lady beetles feed on tiny insects called aphids. Aphids often gather on stems or beneath leaves where they can take in plant juices. A lady beetle can crawl along those parts of the plant searching for a meal. Its young can eat aphids too, even though they do not look like the round adult beetles. A growing lady beetle changes shape before it becomes an adult.
facts: Different kinds of lady beetles have different spot patterns, and some do not have spots.

questions.text: How can several food chains link into a web?
Which other flying insect spent part of its life looking quite different?
What can a leafcutter bee leave on a leaf?

entries.title: What is a red-winged blackbird showing from a marsh stem?
entries.answer: A male red-winged blackbird may perch on a tall marsh stem, sing, and spread the red and yellow patches on his shoulders. From a distance those colors can make him easier for other birds to notice. He can also cover much of the patch when he holds his wings differently. Females often look streaked brown instead. Their colors and the marsh grasses can make them harder to see around the nest.
facts: Red-winged blackbirds often place nests low among marsh plants.

questions.text: What kinds of plants make perches above a shallow marsh?
How can a tiny bright shape be seen on a tall plant?
How do birds find places to hide or hold their nests?

entries.title: What makes a cheetah such a fast runner?
entries.answer: A cheetah is built to run fast for a short stretch. Its legs are long and its back can bend and straighten as it runs. Each time its back stretches out, its feet cover more ground. Its claws grip the dirt, and its long tail helps it balance when its path changes quickly. A cheetah usually tries to get fairly close before starting a chase, because its speed only gives it an advantage for a brief time.
facts: Dark marks run from a cheetah’s eyes toward its mouth.
Cheetahs sprint across open ground after animals such as gazelles.

questions.text: How do lions hunt in a different way?
Why does a tiger use stripes for hunting in cover?
How do muscles pull on bones when an animal moves?

entries.title: What makes an ecosystem
entries.answer: An ecosystem includes living things in a place, the parts of the place that are not alive, and the ways they affect one another. Think of a pond. Sunlight reaches plants and algae in the water. Tiny animals feed on algae, and bigger animals may eat those tiny animals. Bacteria and fungi can break down dead material, making some parts of it available for life to use again. The amount of light, warmth, and water can change which living things do well there. A reef, forest, or puddle can each be an ecosystem.
facts: A food web shows more than one path through which living things get food.
Light and water are parts of an ecosystem even though they are not alive.

questions.text: How do animals and algae help make a reef ecosystem?
Where does the sugar in plants and algae come from?
How can changes in a place affect the traits of living things over generations?

entries.title: What makes long holes in a tree trunk?
entries.answer: A pileated woodpecker uses its strong bill to chip pieces of wood away. It may leave a long, roughly rectangular hole while it searches for carpenter ants and other insects in a trunk or log. Bits of wood can collect on the ground below. The hole it makes for a nest is shaped differently. The nest is up in a tree, where the birds have a sheltered place for their eggs.
facts: A pileated woodpecker is a large black bird with a red crest on top of its head.

questions.text: Why can a downy woodpecker tap without looking for food?
Who may live in an old hole in a snag?
How can a fallen log help young trees grow?

entries.title: Where do shore crabs hide when the tide goes out?
entries.answer: A shore crab on a rocky coast may duck into a narrow crack or shelter beneath a rock as the water drops away. These spots can stay cool and damp while open rock dries in the sun. A crack can also hide the crab from animals that might eat it. Different kinds of shore crab use slightly different parts of the shore. A crab on the open rock can dart sideways to reach cover.
facts: Striped shore crabs on the Pacific coast often shelter in cracks in the rocks.

questions.text: Which little pools hold seawater between tides?
What makes the middle of a mussel bed a place to hide?
Why does a hermit crab carry its hiding place?

entries.title: Where does a dragonfly live before it can fly?
entries.answer: A young dragonfly lives underwater. In this stage it is called an aquatic nymph. It has no working wings yet and can catch other small animals that pass nearby. Some kinds stay underwater for months or longer. When a nymph is ready to become a flying adult, it can climb out on a plant stem. The adult then pulls free from its old skin and opens its new wings.
facts: You may find an empty dragonfly skin clinging to a stem near the water.

questions.text: How do damselfly adults generally hold their wings at rest?
Which other stream insect builds a shelter while young?
How can a water strider skim across the surface?

entries.title: Where does a groundhog spend the winter?
entries.answer: A groundhog, also called a woodchuck, spends the coldest part of the year inside a burrow. It goes into hibernation, when its body cools and its heartbeat and breathing slow down. It uses energy stored as fat from the food it ate before winter. In warmer months, a burrow also offers a groundhog a place to rest and hide. It can have more than one entrance.
facts: A groundhog belongs to the squirrel family, but it spends more of its time on the ground than an eastern gray squirrel.

questions.text: How does a chipmunk save food for winter?
How can a wood frog survive parts of its body freezing?
Why do some animals use the edge between woods and open land?

entries.title: Where does a wild turkey sleep at night?
entries.answer: A wild turkey can spend much of a day walking on the ground. It may scratch through old leaves to find nuts, seeds, or insects. Later it can beat its broad wings and fly up to a branch to spend the night. A spot where a bird rests like this is called a roost. Sleeping above the ground can put the turkey farther from some animals that might hunt it.
facts: Wild turkeys can fly, though they usually travel short distances in the air rather than making long flights.

questions.text: Why can a wood duck’s young leave a high nest before they can fly?
Why are some forest birds found closer to an opening?
What can happen to a nut that a squirrel buries?

entries.title: Why can’t a snapping turtle hide completely in its shell?
entries.answer: A common snapping turtle has a broad shell across its back, but only a small hard area under its body. It cannot tuck all of its head, legs, and tail between those two parts as some other turtles can. In water, a snapping turtle may simply swim or walk away from a disturbance. On land it may defend itself quickly with its strong jaws if it feels trapped.
facts: A snapping turtle has a long tail with raised bumps along the top.

questions.text: Why does a painted turtle climb onto a log?
How can an alligator stay in water with most of its body hidden?
Why can plants and water meet in so many different ways in wetlands?

entries.title: Why do American toad eggs look like long strings?
entries.answer: A female American toad can lay many small dark eggs in a long string of clear jelly. The string can settle among plants in shallow water. The eggs hatch into tadpoles that swim and feed in the water. As they grow, they develop legs and their tails shrink. The little toads can leave the water after they have changed enough to live on land.
facts: Adult American toads have bumpy skin and can live in woods, fields, and gardens.

questions.text: How do spotted salamanders begin life in a pool?
What is a low call you might hear beside a pond?
Why are pond edges useful places for growing animals?

entries.title: Why do birds build nests in so many different places?
entries.answer: Bird nests can sit on the ground, rest in the fork of a tree, or hang like a little bag. A tree cavity can hide a nest, while a hard bank near a river can give another bird room to dig a tunnel. The place has to hold the eggs and young as wind, rain, or animals move around it. Different birds find places that suit the materials they can carry and the way they can reach the nest.
facts: Watching an adult from a distance can show you where it takes building material.

questions.text: Which little bird carries sticks into a tree hole?
Which bird hangs a woven nest from thin twigs?
Which bird digs a long tunnel in a bank?

entries.title: Why do brook trout need cool water?
entries.answer: Brook trout often live in cold, clear streams. Cold water can hold more dissolved oxygen than warm water. Brook trout use their gills to take in that oxygen, and they can struggle when water gets too warm. Streamside trees can shade a stretch of water, and groundwater can also help keep some streams cool. In hot weather, a cooler pool or spring-fed stretch can be especially important.
facts: A brook trout has pale markings along its back and small colored spots along its sides.

questions.text: How can trees beside a stream cool the water?
Why can water run from a hillside without rain?
How can a lake have warmer water above colder water?

entries.title: Why do giant pandas eat so much bamboo?
entries.answer: A giant panda spends much of its day finding and chewing bamboo. Its heavy jaws break tough stems, and a special wrist bone sticks out where a thumb might be. The panda can press a piece of bamboo against its fingers with that bone. Bamboo gives a panda less nourishment than many richer foods would, so the animal eats a great deal of it. In the mountains of central China, pandas move between places where different kinds of bamboo grow.
facts: A panda’s thumb-like grip uses a wrist bone.
Giant pandas belong to the bear family.

questions.text: Why is there a red panda as well as a giant panda?
How do elephants grab leaves when they feed?
What happens to food after an animal swallows it?

entries.title: Why do some fireflies flash in patterns?
entries.answer: Some fireflies make short flashes using a light-making part of the body. The number of flashes and the space between them can form a pattern. Other fireflies of the same species may answer that pattern with their own light. This helps some males and females find one another after dark. Not every kind of firefly makes the same signal, and some adult fireflies do not flash at all.
facts: In a few kinds of firefly, many males can flash at nearly the same time.

questions.text: How can an animal make its own light?
Which animals visit flowers in the dark?
How can city lights affect birds that fly at night?

entries.title: Why do some young caddisflies carry cases made of stones?
entries.answer: Some young caddisflies build a small tube around their soft bodies. They use silk to hold together bits of sand, tiny stones, or pieces of stems found nearby. The caddisfly case protects the body as the insect drags it along while it crawls on the bottom. If it is disturbed, it may pull its head and front legs inside. Other kinds of young caddisflies make shelters that stay in one place.
facts: Some caddisflies use silk to make nets that catch food drifting past instead of carrying a case.

questions.text: What is a stream riffle?
How does a hermit crab use an empty shell for protection?
Why does a leafcutter bee collect bits of leaves?

entries.title: Why do such small frogs make such loud peeps?
entries.answer: A male spring peeper sends out a high call that can sound like a clear whistle. A pouch of skin under its throat, called a vocal sac, puffs up with air as it calls. The sound can help a female find the calling frog among plants at the edge of the water. When lots of male peepers call close together, it can be hard to pick out just one voice.
facts: Many spring peepers have a dark mark shaped like an X on the back.

questions.text: How can a big bullfrog make a low call instead?
Why can a pool in the woods dry out later in the year?
What is different about young red-backed salamanders?

entries.title: Why do young freshwater mussels ride on fish?
entries.answer: Many freshwater mussels start life as tiny young that spend time attached to a fish. The fish can carry them through the water while they develop. Later they drop away and settle on the bottom. As adults, mussels tend to remain in one small area, pulling water through their bodies to capture tiny bits of food. That is one kind of filter feeding. The fish ride helps young mussels spread away from where their parents live.
facts: Different kinds of freshwater mussel can need different kinds of fish for this part of their lives.

questions.text: How does a mussel cling to an ocean rock?
How do pools and riffles give different stream animals shelter?
Why do plants along a stream matter?

entries.title: Why does a bluegill fan a round patch on the bottom?
entries.answer: A male bluegill can sweep loose material aside with its tail to make a shallow, round nest on the bottom of a pond or lake. Several males may build nests close together. A female can leave eggs in a nest, and the male may guard the eggs and young fish for a time. Shallow water can make the nests easy to see from above when the water is clear.
facts: The dark patch on the side of a bluegill’s head lies at the back of its gill cover.

questions.text: Which fish can wait hidden among plants near the shore?
What makes the edge of a pond a good place for plants?
Which pond animal catches fish from above?

entries.title: Why does a brown creeper start near the bottom of a tree?
entries.answer: A brown creeper can land low on a tree and make its way up, checking cracks with its thin curved beak. Its toes grip the bark, and its stiff tail can press against the trunk like part of a tripod. After reaching partway up or near the top, the bird may fly down to start low on another trunk. The brown marks on its back are easy to miss against rough bark.
facts: The bird finds small animals such as insects and spiders in the bark.

questions.text: Which bird can go down a tree headfirst as it checks for food?
How does another tree-climbing bird use its beak?
Why can cracks in bark be places for small animals to live?

entries.title: Why does a bumblebee buzz while holding a flower?
entries.answer: Some flowers hold pollen inside parts that have tiny openings. A bumblebee can grip the flower and shake it with the muscles it uses for flight. Its wings do not have to flap during this buzz. The shake can loosen the pollen so it falls onto the bee. Some pollen may travel to another flower later. This behavior is called buzz pollination, and it helps flowers such as tomatoes release pollen.
facts: A bumblebee also makes a different buzzing sound while it flies.

What are the holes a leafcutter bee leaves on a leaf?
How can gardens offer food for different pollinators all season?

entries.title: Why does a chimney swift cling upright instead of sitting on a branch?
entries.answer: A chimney swift's short feet can grip rough walls and other steep surfaces. The ends of its stiff tail feathers help brace its body. Those features are useful on the inside of a chimney or hollow tree, but the bird does not sit on a twig the way most songbirds do. A pair may make a shallow nest from little sticks, fastened against an upright surface. The birds spend much of the day flying after small insects.
facts: A swift can use its own sticky saliva to join nest twigs together.

questions.text: Why can a hollow space be a good place for some bird nests?
Which flying insect hunter makes a nest from wet earth?
Which woodland bird also leans on its tail as it climbs?

entries.title: Why does a downy woodpecker tap on a branch?
entries.answer: A downy woodpecker may tap a branch to look for insects under its bark. It can also hit wood in a very quick series called a drum. The sound can tell another woodpecker that it has entered an occupied area or help birds find each other. A thin branch can hold this small bird while it searches for insects, even if that branch is too narrow for a heavier woodpecker.
facts: Downy woodpeckers are small enough to feed on some thick weed stems as well as branches.

questions.text: Which large woodpecker can leave long holes in wood?
Who else might later use a hole made by a woodpecker?
Why do trees near a stream matter to animals?

entries.title: Why does a garter snake flick its tongue?
entries.answer: A common garter snake can pick up tiny traces from the air or ground with its tongue. When the tongue comes back inside, the snake brings those traces to a sensing area in its mouth. This helps it find nearby animals or follow a scent left by another snake. The two tips of the tongue can sample slightly different spots. A quick flick is a way of gathering information about its surroundings.
facts: Common garter snakes can eat several kinds of small animals, including frogs and earthworms.

questions.text: Why does a spring peeper make a sharp call?
How does a fox use a different sense to find hidden animals?
How can a bat locate a flying insect?

entries.title: Why does a great blue heron stand so still in water?
entries.answer: A great blue heron can wade into shallow water on its long legs. It may wait with its neck bent until a fish or other small animal comes close, then quickly reach forward with its pointed bill. Standing quietly can keep the bird from warning nearby prey. A heron may also take slow steps as it hunts. The same long legs help it search without getting most of its body wet.
facts: A great blue heron can nest in the branches of a tree even though it often feeds in water.

questions.text: How does an osprey catch a fish without standing in the water?
What can a duck reach when it feeds with its tail up?
Which fish also waits quietly for prey among plants?

entries.title: Why does a hermit crab borrow a shell?
entries.answer: A hermit crab often carries an empty snail shell on its back. The shell helps cover the soft part of its body. If danger comes close, the crab can pull back into the shell. The shell itself does not grow with the hermit crab. As the crab grows, it may look for a roomier shell and move in when it finds one of the right shape and size.
facts: A hermit crab’s hard front legs stick out when it walks, while the softer back part stays inside.

questions.text: What is a tide pool?
How does a limpet use its own shell?
Why is a horseshoe crab a different kind of animal?

entries.title: Why does a house wren carry sticks into a tiny hole?
entries.answer: A northern house wren can make its nest inside a tree cavity or nest box. It carries many small sticks through the entrance. The sticks form a rough base, and softer material can line the cup that holds the eggs. The nest is mostly hidden, but you may see the bird fly to the opening with another twig in its beak. It can take a lot of trips to build a nest inside a space that looked empty.
facts: Male house wrens may put sticks in more than one possible nest site.

questions.text: What are the differences between an open cup nest and a nest in a hole?
How does a duckling leave its nest in a tree?
Which bird attaches a nest to thin twigs at the outside of a branch?

entries.title: Why does a leafcutter bee cut neat circles from leaves?
entries.answer: A leafcutter bee can use its mouth parts to snip a small, rounded piece from a leaf. The bee carries the piece away rather than eating it. It can fit several pieces together to line tiny rooms in a hollow stem or other narrow opening. In a room it leaves food and an egg. The young bee has its own protected space and a supply of food as it grows.
facts: The bee can leave nearly round or oval openings along the edge of a leaf.

questions.text: How does a bumblebee shake pollen loose?
How can plants support many kinds of helpful insects?
Why does a caddisfly attach little plants or stones to a case?

entries.title: Why does a loon run across the water to take off?
entries.answer: A common loon has powerful feet set far back on its body. That helps it push through the water when it dives to catch fish. The same shape makes it awkward on land. When a loon wants to take off from a lake, you may see it paddle rapidly along the surface while beating its wings. It needs a stretch of open water to gather enough speed for flight.
facts: Loons make nests near the water's edge where they can get in and out more easily.

questions.text: How does moving air help hold wings up?
How does a different water bird get from a tree nest to a pond?
Which bird can catch a fish by diving from the air?

entries.title: Why does a mallard tip its tail into the air?
entries.answer: A mallard can dip its head beneath the surface to reach plants or small animals. If the food is a little deeper, it may tip its whole front end down until the tail points up. This way of feeding is called dabbling. The bird can stay near the surface because it is reaching into shallow water. Other ducks can dive all the way underneath to find food.
facts: A mallard may also walk on land to feed where it finds seeds or other food.

questions.text: What are ducklings doing when they jump from a tree nest?
Why are shallows full of plants around some ponds?
What does a great blue heron do while waiting for fish?

entries.title: Why does a meerkat stand on watch?
entries.answer: Meerkats search for insects and other small animals in open, dry parts of southern Africa. When members of the group dig or look closely at the ground, one may climb onto a high spot and watch for danger. A call can warn the others to run to shelter. Meerkats also dig and use underground tunnels. Their burrows offer a safer place to rest and a retreat from the hot ground during part of the day.
facts: Meerkats belong to the mongoose family.
Strong front claws help meerkats dig.

questions.text: How do the duties of an underground colony differ?
Which larger predator often lives in a group?
How can burrows help an animal that hunts?

entries.title: Why does a northern cardinal have a thick bill?
entries.answer: A northern cardinal uses its thick, pointed bill like a little pair of grips. It can hold a seed and crack its outer coat, then take the softer part inside. Seeds are a frequent part of its food. Cardinals also eat fruit and insects. Both males and females have a point of feathers on top of the head, though the male is usually a much brighter red.
facts: A northern cardinal can stay in the same general area through all seasons instead of making a long trip south.

questions.text: How can a blue jay carry acorns away rather than eat them on the spot?
What does a robin often pull from a lawn?
How does a young plant get started from a seed?

entries.title: Why does a painted turtle sit on a log in the sun?
entries.answer: A painted turtle gets much of its body heat from the world around it. On a sunny day it can climb onto a log and warm up. Spending time in the sun this way is called basking. More than one turtle may use the same good spot. If something startles them, the turtles can slide off the log into the water, where they are quick swimmers.
facts: Painted turtles have colorful stripes on their skin and often red marks along part of the shell.

questions.text: How does a snapping turtle’s shell protect its body?
Why do plants grow in the shallow parts of a pond?
How can sunlight warm a surface?

entries.title: Why does a spotted salamander visit a spring pool?
entries.answer: Spotted salamanders spend much of their lives on land, often out of sight in damp woods. On rainy spring nights, adults may travel to temporary pools where their young can grow. The eggs sit in jelly-like masses in the water. Young salamanders hatch with gills and swim. As they grow, they change to a land-living form and can leave the pool, where the water may be drying up.
facts: A spotted salamander can live far enough from its pool that it needs a safe path between the woods and the water.

questions.text: Why does a vernal pool dry out?
How can wildlife get across a road?
What do plants and animals gain from streamside forests?

entries.title: Why does a Virginia opossum carry babies in a pouch?
entries.answer: A Virginia opossum gives birth to very small young that still need a protected place to grow. The babies crawl into a pouch on their mother’s belly. There they drink milk while they grow bigger. Later, young opossums can ride on their mother’s back as she moves about. An opossum is a marsupial, which means it belongs to a group of mammals whose young are born at a very early stage of development and keep growing while they nurse.
facts: When frightened, a Virginia opossum can go still and look as if it is dead.

questions.text: How does a striped skunk warn an animal to stay away?
What can a raccoon feel with its front paws?
Why does a mother wood duck nest up in a tree?

entries.title: Why does a white-tailed deer lift its tail when it runs?
entries.answer: A white-tailed deer’s tail blends in with its coat when the tail hangs down. If the deer is alarmed, it can lift the tail and show the bright white fur underneath. It may hold the tail up as it bounds away. The flash is easy to see among the trees and can signal danger to other deer. Deer often use places where woods and open land meet.
facts: The spots on a young white-tailed deer can help it blend in with patches of light and shade.

questions.text: Why do some animals find good hiding places at a forest edge?
How does a rabbit’s tail look when it heads for cover?
How can wildlife cross a human road?

entries.title: Why does a wood duckling jump out of a tree?
entries.answer: A wood duck often nests in a tree hole near water. After the eggs hatch, the ducklings can climb to the opening even though they cannot fly yet. When their mother calls from below, they jump down and follow her to water. The tree hole helps shelter eggs while the mother is sitting on them, but the ducklings leave it early so they can swim and search for food.
facts: A female wood duck can also use a wooden nest box with an opening like a tree hole.

questions.text: Where do old nest holes in dead trees come from?
How does a mallard reach food under water?
What kinds of plants help small animals hide near the edge of a pond?

entries.title: Why does an American bullfrog make a low booming call?
entries.answer: A male American bullfrog makes a deep call that can carry across a pond. It pushes air through the sound-making parts of its throat. A vocal sac, or pouch under the lower jaw, can swell and help the call carry. Other bullfrogs can hear it from a distance, which helps them find one another or learn where another male is calling. The calls are especially common in the warmer months.
facts: An American bullfrog is much larger than a spring peeper.

questions.text: Why do spring peepers sound so different?
How can a toad’s eggs look like strings?
How do sounds travel from one place to another?

entries.title: Why does an American eel head back out to sea?
entries.answer: An American eel begins life far out in the Atlantic Ocean in a place called the Sargasso Sea. Young eels can drift toward the coast, then move into rivers or other coastal waters to grow. Some travel far inland, while others stay closer to salt water. After years of growing, adults leave those places and head out to sea to reproduce. This fish migration goes in a different direction from that of many salmon.
facts: Very young American eels are thin and nearly see-through.

questions.text: Which fish goes back up a river to reproduce?
How can an estuary join two kinds of water?
Where do many young loggerheads feed as they grow?

entries.title: Why does an American kestrel hang in the air over a field?
entries.answer: An American kestrel is a small falcon that can look over grass from a wire or other high perch. It can also face into the wind and move its wings so it stays near one spot while looking down. That gives it time to watch the ground for a mouse or a large insect moving through the grass. If it spots food, the kestrel can drop quickly toward it.
facts: American kestrels can nest inside a tree cavity or another sheltered opening.

questions.text: How does another falcon use a steep dive?
Why does a hummingbird hover beside a flower?
Why are many grasslands clear enough to see across?

entries.title: Why does an American robin stop and look down on a lawn?
entries.answer: An American robin searching short grass often runs a few steps, stops, and studies the ground. It can pull out an earthworm where it finds one. An open lawn gives it room to see, run, and stop. The bird does not eat only worms, though. It also eats insects and fruit. In cooler months, robins often gather with other robins in places where berries and other fruit are available.
facts: The American robin has an orange breast, but it is a different bird from the European robin.

questions.text: Which bird uses a thick bill to crack seeds?
How do old leaves return materials to the soil?
When can late flowers feed insects that visit a garden?

entries.title: Why does an Atlantic salmon return to a river?
entries.answer: Many Atlantic salmon begin life in fresh water. When they grow and their bodies change, they swim downstream and can spend years feeding in the ocean. Adults can return upstream to reproduce in a river, often the one they came from. Eggs develop in gravel where river water can flow around them. Not all Atlantic salmon make the ocean trip. Some populations spend their lives in fresh water.
facts: Some Atlantic salmon survive after laying or fertilizing eggs and can return to a river to reproduce again.

entries.title: Why does an eastern gray squirrel bury nuts?
entries.answer: An eastern gray squirrel can save food by digging a little hole and covering a nut with soil. A hiding place for food is called a cache. It may bury nuts in lots of places instead of putting them all together. When there is less food around, the squirrel can search for what it saved. It uses its memory and its sense of smell to find some of the nuts. A nut that stays in the soil may sprout instead.
facts: A gray squirrel can build a leafy nest high in a tree or use a hole in a trunk.

entries.title: Why is the golden frog bright yellow?
entries.answer: The Panamanian golden frog is a small toad with bright yellow skin that often has dark marks. The bright color can warn other animals that the skin contains chemicals they should avoid. Golden frogs live near streams. Where water makes calls hard to hear, a frog can lift and wave a front foot to send a signal to another frog. A deadly fungus has made these frogs extremely rare in the wild, so carefully managed colonies help protect them.
facts: A golden frog is a type of toad.
Golden frogs can communicate by waving one front foot.

entries.title: Why might a goldfinch visit a flower that is already dry?
entries.answer: An American goldfinch often comes to dry flower heads to reach the seeds left behind. A bird may hang on close to the head and pull out seeds with its short pointed beak. Plants such as thistles, asters, and sunflowers can give it many little pieces of food. During a nesting season, some goldfinches also use soft plant fibers in their nests. A flower can still have a job for a bird after its petals are gone.
facts: Goldfinches feed mainly on seeds.

entries.title: Why would a killdeer act as if its wing were hurt?
entries.answer: A killdeer often lays its eggs in a shallow ground nest instead of high in a tree. If a possible danger comes close, one parent may move away from the eggs with a wing drooping. The bird can make itself easy to notice, drawing attention away from the nest. As it gets farther from the eggs, it can take off normally. This behavior is one way a parent can protect a nest.
facts: Killdeer eggs have markings that can blend in with pebbly ground.
